attempts.bug_summary: When the file contains an AAD prefix but decryption properties do not provide one, the initialized file AAD omits the prefix instead of using the value stored in the file. This affects configurations where the algorithm stores the prefix and does not require it to be supplied externally.

When an AAD prefix is present both in the file and in decryption properties, the configured verifier is skipped if the algorithm also requires the prefix to be supplied externally. This allows a verifier to reject an invalid file prefix only when the prefix is not marked as externally required.

attempts.bug_summary: When an AAD prefix is present both in the file and in decryption properties, the configured verifier is skipped if the algorithm also requires the prefix to be supplied externally. This allows a verifier to reject an invalid file prefix only when the prefix is not marked as externally required.

When both explicit column-key material and key metadata with a key retriever are supplied, the method consults the key retriever instead of preserving the explicit column key. This can replace the configured key or raise an access-denied error even though a valid explicit key was provided.

The reuse validation for encrypted columns only compares key metadata when the incoming metadata is non-null. As a result, a previously configured column-specific decryptor can be reused with missing key metadata without raising the required mismatch exception.
